title: Why Guests Still Call When Everything Is on the Website
summary: Only 54.2% of DACH hotels can finish a booking on their own site. 82% of hotels with no online path still have a live website. Why guests call when the page looks complete.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### Why do hotel guests still call if the information is on the website?


Because a published page and a finished request are different jobs. A website can show hours, rates, and room types and still be unable to complete a booking, issue an invoice, grant an exception, or produce a live access fact such as tonight's door code.


In an enrichment of 26,707 hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland with live websites (June 2026), only 54.2% run a real direct-booking engine, and 6.5% tell guests on the hotel's own site to book by phone. Guests call when the page stops short of the last step, not only when the page is empty.


### How many hotels can actually be booked on their own website?


In that same 26,707-hotel DACH enrichment, only 54.2% run a real direct-booking engine, which means nearly half cannot be booked instantly on their own site. Another 8.5% have no online booking path at all, and 82% of those sit on a perfectly live website. Up to 37.3% are present on an online travel agency with no engine of their own.


Detection is a floor: it depends on what the hotel publishes, and a non-standard engine can be missed.


### What do hotel websites tell guests to do when they cannot book online?


A large share send the guest to the phone. At least 13.3% of the 26,707 hotels confirm bookings by manual callback, and 6.5% emphasize phone-to-book on the hotel's own website. Both figures are lower bounds.


The other common door is an agency listing: 73.8% of the same hotels already carry a Booking.com page, and the median hotel lists on three agencies, so a guest who cannot finish on the hotel site can usually finish somewhere else.


### Why can't a hotel website replace the phone?


The website was built to publish. The phone is asked to finish work the page cannot close: a live access fact, an invoice, a change to an existing booking, an exception to a written policy, or a price that does not match another channel. Better pages close the look-up. They do not close judgment, identity, or a fact that is only true tonight.


Published information can also be[out of date in the system that feeds the site](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/why-your-hotels-information-goes-stale) , but even a current page still leaves those request types unfinished.


### How can a hotel tell if its website is finishing guest requests?


Test the last step, not the look of the page. Try to book tonight on the hotel's own site and see whether the next step is a completed reservation or a form, a callback promise, or a phone number. Ask one question the page does not answer and see whether the published content closes it. Compare the homepage rate with the first agency listing.


If the hotel runs several properties, run the same booking attempt on each site. A page that looks complete and still ends on a phone number is not finishing the job.
